mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate signals a strong labor market, which increases consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following low UNRATE values.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate above 0.1 signals monetary tightening, which may reduce borrowing and spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day windows following FEDFUNDS increases above 0.1.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth (GDPC1) is strong and unemployment (UNRATE) is low, it indicates a robust economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the 60-day windows following strong GDP growth and low UNRATE.

mechanism_narrative: A peak in industrial production (INDPRO) may signal a supply chain slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 60% of the 20-day windows following an INDPRO peak.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts (HOUST) indicate strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following increased HOUST.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 50% of the 20-day windows following significant PAYEMS increases.

mechanism_narrative: When inflation (CPIAUCSL) rises and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) increases, it may signal tighter monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 30% of the 60-day windows following CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS increases.

mechanism_narrative: A low and stable inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) may lead to accommodative monetary policy, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following low CPIAUCSL.
